edges.description: DBP is used as the means of suppressing fetal Leydig cell steroidogenesis, so the model manipulates this node rather than arising from it spontaneously.
edges.limitations: Phthalate suppression of fetal Leydig steroidogenesis is species specific. Rats show it, mice do not, and grafted human fetal testis does not either, so this link supports a mechanism that human tissue has not been shown to share at the steroidogenic step.

edges.description: The rat model reproduces the somatic and masculinisation arms of TDS but not the germ cell neoplasia arm: GCNIS cells and human-type germ cell cancers have not been described in any animal model of TDS. The model does reproduce the focal dysgenetic histology seen in the testes of men with GCNIS, so it speaks to the lesion's context without reproducing the neoplastic lesion itself.
edges.limitations: Likely a species difference in male gonad development. Any inference from this model to the cancer component of TDS passes through the shared dysgenetic histology, not through a modelled neoplasm, and the latency and post-pubertal proliferation that produce human invasive cancer are not represented at all.

edges.limitations: A mouse germline receptor variant, not an environmental exposure, so it models the descent mechanism rather than the environmental aetiology TDS is usually framed around. Recessive RXFP2 variants do cause familial bilateral cryptorchidism in humans (PMID:31167797), but that is a rare Mendelian presentation; the INSL3-RXFP2 axis is not established as a common cause of sporadic human cryptorchidism.

nodes.description: The initiating event of the TDS hypothesis as the rat data actually constrain it: a single early, DBP-sensitive disturbance of fetal testis set-up, probably at the level of somatic cell lineage specification, which independently produces fetal Leydig cell failure, Sertoli cell dysfunction and the focal dysgenetic lesion. Its primary causes may be environmental anti-androgens, genetic lesions of androgen signalling, or unknown factors. The node is deliberately placed upstream of all three rather than making dysgenesis the cause of somatic dysfunction: in the rat, Leydig cell impairment is present before dysgenesis is detectable, and the authors who measured both read their correlation as a shared origin rather than one causing the other.

nodes.description: Insufficient androgen receptor signalling in reproductive tract target tissues during a discrete fetal window (rat embryonic day 15.5 to 18.5; postulated human equivalent around 8 to 14 weeks of gestation). Androgen action inside this window, and not during the later period of morphological differentiation, is what programmes masculinisation of the whole reproductive tract in the rat. Anogenital distance is set within the same window, which is what makes it a read-out of androgen action here rather than of androgen levels at any later time.

evidence.reference_title: Identification in rats of a programming window for reproductive tract masculinization, disruption of which leads to hypospadias and cryptorchidism.
evidence.snippet: We exposed rat fetuses to either anti-androgens or androgens and showed that masculinization of all reproductive tract tissues was programmed by androgen action during a common fetal programming window.

evidence.snippet: Based on the timings in rats, we believe the programming window in humans is likely to be 8-14 weeks of gestation.

nodes.description: Interruption of the first stage of testicular descent, in which the testis is held near the inguinal region as the abdomen grows. In the mouse it carries spermatogenic consequences in its own right, up to Sertoli-cell-only tubules. Human descent has two phases and this node models only the INSL3-dependent trans-abdominal one; the later inguinoscrotal phase is androgen-dependent and reaches cryptorchidism through Incomplete Reproductive Tract Masculinization instead, so human cryptorchidism is not attributed wholly to this node.

nodes.description: Impaired steroidogenic function of the fetal Leydig cells, the proximate consequence of testis maldevelopment and the step that limits androgen available to the masculinisation programming window. In the dibutyl phthalate rat, intratesticular testosterone falls during exposure and recovers if exposure stops at the end of the window, which is why a late testosterone measurement can miss the deficit that matters.

nodes.description: The structural signature of the early disruption: focal areas in which Leydig cells form large aggregates, Sertoli cells sit ectopically outside the seminiferous cords, and cords are malformed, with intratubular Leydig cells appearing after birth. It is a marker of poor set-up during the programming window rather than a cause of the downstream disorders, which is why it carries no downstream edges: it is not even detectable until after the window in which the damage is done. The same focal changes are found in the testes of men with germ cell neoplasia in situ.

evidence.reference_title: Inter-relationship between testicular dysgenesis and Leydig cell function in the masculinization programming window in the rat.
evidence.snippet: DBP-induced focal testicular dysgenesis (Leydig cell aggregation, ectopic Sertoli cells, malformed seminiferous cords) is not evident until after the MPW.

evidence.reference_title: Inter-relationship between testicular dysgenesis and Leydig cell function in the masculinization programming window in the rat.
evidence.snippet: Focal testicular dysgenesis is simply a reflection of poor set-up during this early programming period, even though it is not observed itself until some time later in development.

nodes.description: The preinvasive lesion, historically carcinoma in situ, in which the arrested germ cells persist within the seminiferous tubules of the postnatal and adult testis. It is the precursor of most invasive testicular germ cell tumours, and the testes that carry it show the same focal dysgenetic changes as the rat model.

evidence.reference_title: Experimentally induced testicular dysgenesis syndrome originates in the masculinization programming window.
evidence.snippet: We related our findings to human TDS cases by demonstrating similar focal dysgenetic changes in testes of men with preinvasive germ cell neoplasia (GCNIS) and in testes of DBP-MPW animals.

nodes.description: Pregnant rats exposed to di(n-butyl) phthalate, which suppresses fetal testicular testosterone production. The model's decisive feature is window specificity: DBP suppresses fetal testosterone equally during and after the masculinisation programming window, but only exposure inside the window shortens anogenital distance and produces focal testicular dysgenesis and the TDS disorders. It is the model that converted TDS from a hypothesis into a testable, and tested, causal claim.

evidence.reference_title: Experimentally induced testicular dysgenesis syndrome originates in the masculinization programming window.
evidence.snippet: If our results are translatable to humans, they suggest that identification of potential causes of human TDS disorders should focus on exposures during a human MPW equivalent, especially if negatively associated with offspring AGD.

nodes.description: Pregnant rats exposed to flutamide, an androgen receptor antagonist, which blocks androgen action at the receptor rather than suppressing its synthesis. This separates the receptor-level step from the steroidogenic step: flutamide and DBP both shorten anogenital distance and reduce androgen-dependent organ size, but flutamide does so without reducing testosterone production. Single-dose dosing on individual gestational days further resolves which day programmes which structure.
nodes.id: Gestational flutamide rat model of androgen receptor blockade

evidence.reference_title: Changes in androgen-mediated reproductive development in male rat offspring following exposure to a single oral dose of flutamide at different gestational ages.
evidence.snippet: Thus, a single gestational exposure of flutamide induced numerous reproductive tract malformations consistent with previously reports following multiple exposures, with the timing of the exposure producing marked tissue selectivity in the response noted in adult offspring.

nodes.description: Ventral displacement of the urethral meatus, the second congenital component of TDS and, like cryptorchidism, inducible in the rat only by androgen disruption inside the programming window.

nodes.description: A second, androgen-independent route from fetal Leydig cell dysfunction to a TDS component. Insulin-like 3 (INSL3), made by the fetal Leydig cells, acts through its receptor RXFP2 on the gubernaculum, the ligament anchoring the testis to the lower abdomen. Signalling through this axis drives myogenic differentiation and maintains androgen-receptor-positive cells in the gubernaculum, with Wnt/beta-catenin and Notch as downstream pathways. Loss of the ligand or the receptor interrupts the first, trans-abdominal stage of descent, which is why cryptorchidism can arise from Leydig cell failure without a proportionate deficit in testosterone.

nodes.description: The organism-level consequence of deficient androgen action in the programming window: under-virilisation of the androgen-dependent reproductive structures. In the rat, which is where this node's evidence comes from, it presents as hypospadias, altered penile length and reduced ventral prostate and seminal vesicle size, all tracking with anogenital distance. The corresponding human components of TDS are hypospadias and cryptorchidism, but that correspondence is inferred from the shared endocrinology rather than measured in humans.

nodes.description: The invasive malignancy that develops from GCNIS after puberty, and the most severe component of TDS. It is the distal endpoint of the germ cell arm, matching the organism-level endpoints the androgen and descent arms reach.

evidence.snippet: We describe a rare family with 3 males affected by a mild disorder of sex determination compatible with testicular dysgenesis syndrome (TDS), including subfertility, cryptorchidism, hypospadias, and testicular cancer, caused by a novel AR mutation.

nodes.description: The second environmental exposure with both human and rodent support. Mild analgesics are prostaglandin synthesis inhibitors with anti-androgenic activity. Maternal use during pregnancy is associated dose-dependently with congenital cryptorchidism in one of two Nordic birth cohorts, and paracetamol use specifically within the 8 to 14 week window is associated with shorter infant anogenital distance. In rats the same exposure shortens AGD and reduces testosterone production by fetal testis ex vivo, which supplies the mechanism the human associations lack.

nodes.description: Anti-androgenic phthalate diesters are the best-characterised environmental cause of the TDS phenotype. In rodents, gestational exposure suppresses fetal testicular testosterone and shortens anogenital distance; in humans, prenatal urinary phthalate metabolite concentrations are inversely related to infant anogenital index at exposure levels common in the general population.

evidence.reference_title: Decrease in anogenital distance among male infants with prenatal phthalate exposure.
evidence.snippet: The age-adjusted AGI decreased significantly with increasing phthalate score (p-value for slope = 0.009).

evidence.snippet: These data support the hypothesis that prenatal phthalate exposure at environmental levels can adversely affect male reproductive development in humans.

nodes.description: A mouse carrying an ENU-induced missense change in leucine-rich repeat 8 of Rxfp2, the INSL3 receptor. The variant leaves total protein near normal but markedly reduces cell-surface expression and caps the maximum cAMP response, so it is a partial loss-of-function of receptor trafficking rather than a null. Genetic complementation against a loss-of-function allele confirmed causality. It isolates the descent arm of TDS from the androgen arm, and shows that a descent defect alone brings spermatogenic damage with it.

evidence.reference_title: Suppression of insulin-like3 receptor reveals the role of beta-catenin and Notch signaling in gubernaculum development.
evidence.snippet: Deletion of Insl3 or its receptor, Rxfp2, in mice causes cryptorchidism.

nodes.description: Malfunction of the Sertoli cells, the nurse cells on which germ cell differentiation depends. In the dysgenetic fetal testis Sertoli cells are mislocated outside the seminiferous cords; after birth the affected foci develop malformed cords containing intratubular Leydig cells, and these persist for life as Sertoli-cell-only tubules. Disturbed Sertoli-germ cell signalling is the proposed route by which dysgenesis reaches the germ cell lineage.
